I'd like to share an Aristotle authored project I thought was pretty cool: https://github.com/Timeroot/Z80Emu
The main point is, Aristotle can verify software on a foreign architecture with no aid from existing software verification API.

The first request was asking Aristotle to formalize a Z80 emulator, which it did. Then, I asked it to make an assembler, and write some test programs in assembly (fibonacci, gcd, etc.) which it did, and they worked correctly. Then I asked it to prove correctness: this turned out to be a trivial native_decide proof since they operated on byte-size words and could be immediately brute-force checked.

So here was the kicker: I asked it to write a BigNum implementation and use that for GCD, and verify that.

It programmed this in assembly, and verified (by evaluation) some randomly chosen values.

The bulk of the work then came verifying this. ~80 assembly instructions, no existing libraries or data types of even a notion of "memory safety" or "loop", not even the guarantee that the code wouldn't modify itself; any program verification has to model the whole CPU execution.

After 14 rounds of submitting to Aristotle (without editing the prompt), it got it! It was smart enough to talk about the basic operations here (like the comparison and subtract subroutine and so on) and prove them individually, https://github.com/Timeroot/Z80Emu/blob/main/Z80Emu/CmpLoopProof.lean and then it worked! :) I'm pleasantly surprised, I genuinely thought this would be much harder.
The code is an absolute mess and I'm well aware of that. I've deliberately left it that way as an artifact
Wow the embedded assembly (e.g. bigGcdProgram) is really interesting!
I realized that the main result is not super easy to find in the repo, it's here: https://github.com/Timeroot/Z80Emu/blob/fc531c4fb19b9a7c5129914a22be1e8475b9052d/Z80Emu/BigNumGCDZ80Proof.lean#L493
Can we get it to correctly formalise an accurate NES emulator?? https://github.com/100thCoin/AccuracyCoin
I think that test suites are a great way to keep AIs anchored and goal oriented, so... Probably!
